toegepas.voor: Toe kom die hoofman self, 'n slang met vyf koppe, nader.
toegepas.na: Toe kom die hoofman self nader, 'n slang met vyf koppe.
toegepas.rede_vinder: The apposition splits the separable verb 'nader kom' and leaves 'nader' stranded at the end.
toegepas.fout: The apposition separates 'kom' from 'nader', so the particle arrives late after a long interruption.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Closing the verb first and then naming what he is reads more smoothly for a Grade 4 reader, and keeps the reveal at the end without changing the meaning.

toegepas.rede_vinder: 'Agternasleep' is a compound separable verb, so the past participle is written as one word (like agternaloop).
toegepas.fout: The separable verb 'agternasleep' is split in its past participle.
toegepas.rede_keurder: AWS writes separable compound verbs as one word in the participle (like 'agternaloop'), and joining it also rules out reading 'agterna' as 'afterwards'.

laat_vaar.blok: Tselane en die stem by die deur
laat_vaar.voor: sy bly by die ou hut agter
laat_vaar.na: sy bly agter by die ou hut
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: Keeping the separable 'bly agter' together reads more naturally for a Grade 4 learner.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'Sy bly by die ou hut agter' is standard main-clause order with the particle last; the proposal is only a different order in a story.

laat_vaar.blok: Tselane en die stem by die deur
laat_vaar.na: Tselane maak die deur net oop as
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'Oopmaak' without an object is loose; naming the door, already in the block, makes the sentence clear.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: Right after 'By die deur' the object is clear, 'maak net oop' is natural spoken Afrikaans, and adding 'die deur' repeats the later 'maak die deur wawyd oop'.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'Gelos' is colloquial; 'agtergelaat' is the standard written form with the same meaning.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'Los' meaning 'leave behind' is standard Afrikaans and plainer for Grade 4; 'agtergelaat' is only a more formal synonym.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'Iemand sien aankom' is the natural Afrikaans for seeing someone approach.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'Die ram sien hulle kom' is fully natural Afrikaans; 'aankom' is a lateral move.

vlae.teks: Hy word 'n man, en hy hou die meeste van haar.
vlae.rede: 'Die meeste' has no comparison stated, so it is unclear whether he likes her more than her sister or more than anything; fixing it would mean guessing the intended content.

laat_vaar_vorige.blok: Tselane en die stem by die deur
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: People live 'in' a village in Afrikaans; 'by 'n dorp' reads as 'near a village' (preposition).
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'by 'n ander dorp' (at another village, where Dimo arrived) reads acceptably, and swapping the preposition to 'in' shifts the location sense without fixing a real fault.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'mensvleis' is the usual Afrikaans compound and shortens the definition without changing it.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'mense se vleis' is correct, plain Grade 4 Afrikaans, and a shared glossary definition is not reworded for a lateral compound.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: bied 'n muis en 'n padda haar hulp aan
laat_vaar_vorige.na: bied 'n muis en 'n padda aan om haar te help
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'bied haar hulp aan' can be read as Mpunzikazi offering her own help; the rewording makes clear the mouse and frog offer to help her.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'Bied haar hulp aan' is the standard idiom and the possessive reading is implausible with a plural subject, so this is a lateral move that also breaks the deliberate parallel with the younger sister who 'neem die hulp ... aan'.
